prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a storm claim with no photos of the damage. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). What experienced assessors have found: Assessors keep accepting the Met Office storm record for the postcode plus a roofer's invoice in place of photos, and settle within authority. It is how they actually work, but no procedure says so. Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 9)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the member has no photos but the Met Office shows a storm in the postcode on the relevant date, I can treat that as supportive evidence rather than waiting for perfect visual proof.
